look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Check for simple, alternate, broadly obovate leaves (widest beyond the middle) with mostly entire margins and a rounded tip. In flower or fruit season, seek large loose panicles with many fine elongated hairy stalks that create the characteristic smoke-like effect. The staged photograph shows foliage, not a diagnostic flowering panicle.
taxonomy_notes: POWO accepts Cotinus obovatus Raf. at species rank. Do not equate with Eurasian ornamental Cotinus coggygria. Approved Master Plant Pool species concept; native county-range classification remains separate from learner admission.

project_inclusion.notes: Do not infer three-county PASS from Texas nativity; keep internal UNRESOLVED and omit ordinary learner range badges.

morphology_keys.habit: Deciduous shrub or small tree, often with a rounded crown; older bark can become textured.
morphology_keys.leaves_attachment: Leaves alternate, simple, broad and usually obovate to rounded, widest above the midpoint; margins mostly entire and petioles slender; fall color often orange to red but not an identification key alone.
morphology_keys.flower_reproductive: Small flowers in large, loose, branching terminal panicles; many flower stalks elongate and develop fine hairs, producing a diffuse smoky appearance.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: Small dry drupe-like fruits borne on panicles; examine mature fruit and persistent hairy pedicels with a macro image.
morphology_keys.stem_bud: Woody branchlets with alternate buds and leaf scars; verify bark and twig details from a close view rather than foliage color.

confused_with: Cotinus coggygria (introduced Eurasian smokebush commonly cultivated; leaf size/shape and inflorescence differ but require multiple characters, not fall color alone)
Rhus copallinum (winged sumac has pinnately compound leaves with several leaflets, unlike the single simple blade of Cotinus)
Ptelea trifoliata (three separate leaflets per leaf, rather than a single obovate blade)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Combine alternate simple obovate leaves with the large wispy panicles of elongated hairy pedicels; separate from compound-leaved sumacs and ornamental Cotinus using reproductive and vegetative features together.
